Despite the blowout print and Q2 guidance of $91B, the stock is trading at $220.30 on May 21, down roughly 1.4% from the post-earnings close of $223.47, reflecting the now-familiar pattern of “sell the news” that has characterized multiple recent NVDA prints. [...] The setup is straightforward but not without risk. NVDA is compounding on an already enormous revenue base at ~85% YoY growth, which is historically unprecedented at this scale. Continued execution on Vera Rubin and a potential China re-entry via H200 licenses would be the next incremental catalysts. However, the market’s consistent “sell the news” reaction, stretched valuations (market cap ~$5.4T), and geopolitical unpredictability around China export controls remain the primary overhangs [...] No downgrades were recorded in the April-May 2026 window across the data returned.
